research_concepts: PULL_UP as a counter to defensive scheme
methodological_questions: Is 'PNR fail' defined from pre-possession or training-period information rather than from the outcome?
What is the unit, and what baseline defines lift, so that general defensive quality is not counted as a PULL_UP effect?
Are the 70%-positive and median >2pp thresholds achievable given per-unit noise and exposure?
How are regression to the mean, shooter selection and shot difficulty handled?
Is there a placebo counter play type, and how is multiplicity across counters handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Descriptive comparison of regular season vs playoffs across 25 defensive teams. PULL_UP PPP allowed rose by +0.341 and its share fell by 7.6pp. PNR PPP changed by -0.139 and its share rose by 12.1pp. No inferential test was run. The record says the PNR share jump may reflect tagging differences, and flags LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR.

Matchup decomposition on 4 playoff games. Team-PT lifts were small, with PNR +1.2pp in one series and -4.1pp in another. Player-channel lifts were large but rested on n of about 15-54. The record lists insufficient exposure and exposure sparsity, and notes helper steals in the primary-defender attribution and no holdout.
Sweep of 870 team pairs. Defense edges versus the league depended only on the defense (for example DAL PNR +9.2% against every offense), so they were not matchup-specific. No validation was recorded.

Pre-game play-type ranking from training data predicted held-out efficiency ranking (median rho +0.539; 90.8% positive lift) over 908 game-team rows. The record's caveat is that the top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types. The record also lists DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY and a C_artifact failure mechanism.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player- and team-level lift estimates from a handful of playoff games
failed_approaches.why: Insufficient exposure (A_unanswerable, LIM:insufficient_exposure). Cells had n of 15-54, helper steals contaminated defender attribution, and there was no holdout.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating defense-only edges against the league as opponent-specific exploitable weaknesses
failed_approaches.why: The edges depend only on the defense, so they are not matchup-specific. The failure mechanism is recorded as unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading PT PPP and share shifts as evidence of suppression or counters
failed_approaches.why: No inferential test. Tagging and label differences and mechanical floor effects are flagged as possible explanations, and the mechanism is unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using top play-type lift as evidence of meaningful discrimination
failed_approaches.why: Part of the lift reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types (C_artifact).

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record directly tests whether PULL_UP is a counter after PNR failure, so the question has not been answered.
Play-type PPP and share data exist and can be computed for 25 teams, and a training-to-holdout ranking design has been run (FAM:SF-APPA-063, status supported).
Small-n cells (n around 15-54) and defense-only effects have produced uninterpretable or non-specific results (FAM:SF-APPA-066, FAM:SF-APPA-034).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP lift after PNR failure is positive in at least 70% of units or has median above 2pp.
Whether PNR failure can be defined from non-outcome information.
Whether any PULL_UP lift exceeds that of other play types (a placebo comparison).
Whether PULL_UP results are stable across seasons or between the regular season and playoffs, or free of tagging error.
own_inferences: Without a baseline that removes overall defensive quality, a bad PNR defense will tend to show positive lift for every play type. The lift would then be a defense-quality effect, not a PULL_UP-specific one.
If PNR failure is defined from realised PNR outcomes and PULL_UP is then measured on the same possessions or games, the result is outcome-derived and mechanical. A temporal split is needed.

The 70%-positive criterion depends on per-unit noise. If the per-unit SE is about 3pp and the true lift is 0, about 50% of units will be positive. A true lift of about 2pp gives about 75% positive, so both criteria together are only barely reachable.
Regular season and playoff data should not be pooled, given the tagging and share shifts in FAM:SF-APPS-012.
uncertainties: The meaning of 'unit' (team-season, game, player or matchup) and the definition of 'PNR fail' are unspecified.
Per-unit PULL_UP possession counts are unknown.
Tagging consistency of the derived play-type records across seasons is unknown.
The 2025-26 playoffs are partial on the question date and complete only on 2026-06-21.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I might have proceeded as posed. The records show that small-n cells, defense-only effects and tagging and label problems break this kind of work, so I moved to proceed_with_changes. The changes are a non-outcome definition of failure, a temporal holdout, a differential baseline, a placebo play type, and a minimum possession threshold.

blocking_constraints.text: 'PNR fail' is undefined. If it is defined by the outcome of the same possessions, the test is circular.
If the unit is game- or matchup-level, PULL_UP counts per unit are too small. Units must be team-seasons, or pooled, with a minimum possession count.

prior_work.summary: The retrieved families are descriptive or adjacent. They show the data support PT PPP and share analysis, and that small-n and defense-only effects mislead. None tests PULL_UP lift conditional on PNR failure.

risks.text: Defining PNR failure from realised PNR efficiency makes PULL_UP lift mechanically related to the label.
Defense quality, shot difficulty, shooter quality and opponent strength all affect pull-up efficiency. Without a differential baseline, lift reflects defense quality.
Units selected for extreme PNR failure will regress toward the mean, and that regression can show up as a lift.
The per-unit SE of the lift may be about as large as the 2pp effect threshold. The 70% criterion is sensitive to noise.
Small cells (n around 15-54 in FAM:SF-APPA-066) cannot support unit-level estimates.
PT tagging differences across seasons or between regular season and playoffs (FAM:SF-APPS-012) can create spurious changes.
A change in PT share or PPP can arise mechanically from how possessions are classified.
Several counters and thresholds are implied, so a PULL_UP-only test overstates specificity unless the other counters are included.
Without a placebo play type, a positive PULL_UP lift cannot be separated from a general lift on all play types.
Defensive schemes and league tendencies drift across four seasons, which affects the holdout comparison.
The positive-lift base rate under the null is about 50%. The criterion needs a null calibration, not a comparison to zero.

design.estimand: Differential PULL_UP lift for defenses with PNR failure. Step 1: in a training window, classify defense-team-seasons as PNR-failing if PNR PPP allowed is above the league baseline by a pre-set margin (for example the worst tercile), using possessions in the training window only. Step 2: in a disjoint holdout window, lift = [PULL_UP PPP (or points per attempt) against the defense minus league PULL_UP PPP] minus [all-play-type PPP against the defense minus league all-play-type PPP]. As a secondary estimate, compute the same quantity for matched non-failing defenses.
design.unit: Defense team-season, with 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons as units and training and holdout splits by game date within season, or prior-half versus later-half. Player- and game-level units are excluded as underpowered.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (complete from 2026-04-13). Playoffs are analysed separately, and 2025-26 playoffs are excluded until complete (2026-06-21). Include only units with at least N PULL_UP possessions in the holdout window (threshold to be fixed before looking, for example 150). Report how many units are excluded.
design.power: Before the confirmatory run, simulate per-unit SE from the empirical PULL_UP possession counts. Compute the probability of passing both criteria (at least 70% positive and median above 2pp) when the true lift is 0, 2pp and 4pp. If the null passes more than 5% of the time or the 2pp scenario passes less than 80% of the time, declare underpowered and report an interval instead. Use a cluster bootstrap over teams for CIs on the share positive and the median.
design.controls: Control for opponent offensive quality, shooter identity or shooter quality prior, shot distance and defender-distance proxies where available, score and clock state, home/away and season. Use a team-season-demeaned baseline. Check for regression to the mean by comparing against a randomly assigned label and against matched non-failing teams. Audit PT tagging consistency by season, and keep regular season and playoffs separate.
design.falsification: Placebo counters: compute the same lift for SPOT_UP, DRIVE and CUT. PULL_UP is supported as a specific counter only if its lift exceeds the placebo lifts. Shuffle PNR-failure labels across defenses to get the null distribution of share positive and median lift. Run a pre-period test in which a label from a later window should not predict an earlier window.
design.multiplicity: PULL_UP is the single pre-registered primary counter. Other play types are secondary and reported with Holm correction. The thresholds (70% and 2pp) are fixed in advance and no alternatives are searched.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if all of the following hold: share of units with lift above 0 is at least 70% with the lower bootstrap CI bound above 60%; median lift is above 2pp with the CI excluding 0; the result is stable across at least three of four seasons; PULL_UP beats the placebo lifts; and the label-shuffle null fails the criteria. Rejected if the power check passes and the criteria are not met. Untestable if the power check fails. Artifact if the result disappears under the differential baseline or the label shuffle.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and derived play-type possession records as available on 2026-05-23: 2022-23 to 2024-25 complete, 2025-26 regular season complete, 2025-26 playoffs partial and excluded. Record the extraction date, graph database build and tagging version, and freeze them before analysis.

research_concepts: pull-up jump shot as counter to defensive scheme
methodological_questions: How is PNR failure defined and is the label derived from the outcome?
What is the unit of analysis and the baseline for lift (pp) in pull-up efficiency?
Is a 70% of units with lift>0 and median lift>2pp threshold powered given sparse exposure per unit?
How to control for regression to the mean, selection of shooters, and confounding by shot difficulty and defender?
Is there a placebo or comparison counter strategy to establish PULL_UP specificity, and how to handle multiple testing across counters?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether another tool call is worth it, but I think I can wrap up now. The key constraint is the date: the 2025-26 playoffs aren't complete as of the question's date, so I'm limiting the data to the regular seasons from 2022-23 through 2025-26 and leaving out that partial playoff run.

Next I'm checking the recorded statuses for the four appendix items, and the evidence behind each: the PULL_UP and PNR share shifts in one, the small sample sizes in another, and the way the edges depend only on the defense in a third. I'm also thinking through how to define a "PNR failure" so it comes from information available before the possession, not the outcome, and how to measure the PULL_UP lift against the baseline.

I'm settling on a concrete lift definition: compare each defense's pull-up efficiency against the league pull-up baseline, then subtract its overall shortfall, so a generally weak defense doesn't look like a pull-up effect. I'm also considering a placebo comparison using other shot types and thresholds on the unit count, since roughly 120 team-seasons may be thin for the pull-up possessions per defense.

I'm now estimating the noise: with roughly 400 possessions per defense, the standard error on a pull-up efficiency gap comes out near 3 percentage points per unit, so a true lift of about 2 points would show up as positive in only around three-quarters of units, and a true zero lift would give about half. That means the 70% threshold effectively requires a real effect of about 1.6 points or more.

I'm settling on the final probability estimates now: the outcome categories sit at roughly 20% supported, 20% rejected, 10% untestable, 20% artifact, and 30% uncertain, with a decision to proceed with changes and about a 55% chance the question is testable.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether another tool call is worth it, but I think I can wrap up now. The key constraint is the date: the 2025-26 playoffs aren't complete as of the question's date, so I'm limiting the data to the regular seasons from 2022-23 through 2025-26 and leaving out that partial playoff run.

Next I'm checking the recorded statuses for the four appendix items, and the evidence behind each: the PULL_UP and PNR share shifts in one, the small sample sizes in another, and the way the edges depend only on the defense in a third. I'm also thinking through how to define a "PNR failure" so it comes from information available before the possession, not the outcome, and how to measure the PULL_UP lift against the baseline.

I'm settling on a concrete lift definition: compare each defense's pull-up efficiency against the league pull-up baseline, then subtract its overall shortfall, so a generally weak defense doesn't look like a pull-up effect. I'm also considering a placebo comparison using other shot types and thresholds on the unit count, since roughly 120 team-seasons may be thin for the pull-up possessions per defense.

I'm now estimating the noise: with roughly 400 possessions per defense, the standard error on a pull-up efficiency gap comes out near 3 percentage points per unit, so a true lift of about 2 points would show up as positive in only around three-quarters of units, and a true zero lift would give about half. That means the 70% threshold effectively requires a real effect of about 1.6 points or more.

I'm settling on the final probability estimates now: the outcome categories sit at roughly 20% supported, 20% rejected, 10% untestable, 20% artifact, and 30% uncertain, with a decision to proceed with changes and about a 55% chance the question is testable.
